newsitem.title: USA: Cooper says comfortable with '97 estimates.
newsitem.headline: Cooper says comfortable with '97 estimates.

text.p: Cooper Companies Inc on Tuesday said it is comfortable it can reach analysts' consensus earnings estimate of $1.55 to $1.65 a share for fiscal 1997, which incldues a $0.15 per share tax benefit.
"I remain comfortable with the previous estimate of $1.55 to $1.65 per share," Chief Executive Thomas Bender said in a statement with Cooper's fiscal 1997 first quarter earnings.
He added the company, which makes and sells speciality health care products, expects earnings per share in each of the next two years "to grow around 40 percent, excluding tax benefits."

Earlier the company reported a first quarter profit of $0.28 a share including a $0.04 per share tax benefit. In the year ago quarter, the company earned $0.06 a share including a tax benefit of $0.01 a share.
Revenues totaled about $28.4 million in fiscal 1997's first quarter versus $22.2 million one year ago.

The company reported increased sales in each of its operating units, contact lens business CooperVision sales grew 21 percent, CooperSurgical sales were up 38 percent, and Hospital Group of America saw its sales rise 31 percent.
